comments.author: Anon
comments.html: The thing that seems strange is the need for these companies to have such an open base to start with. It seems like they should be able to just build on closed Solaris and possibly have a "special relationship" with Oracle to feed in their changes (clearly they've got the engineering talent to need such a set up). If open is better than why isn't FreeBSD ten times better than Windows on a server (although I am saying this as a Linux user not a developer)?

comments.author: ahl
comments.html: FreeBSD _is_ ten times better than Windows for an appliance. Why don't companies license code from Oracle? Oracle probably doesn't want to do it, and companies wouldn't want to bet their future on Oracle's eternal beneficence.
